title: Composition by equivalences on Segal mapping spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and Reedy fibrancy from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $V:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be Reedy fibrant with consecutive-edge maps $V_n\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ weak homotopy equivalences for $n\geq2$. For vertices $x,y$, put $M(x,y)=\operatorname{fib}_{(x,y)}((d_1,d_0):V_1\to V_0^2)$, and use the homotopy category $hV$ and invertible components described in [lem-coef-segal-homotopy-category-components]. A simplicial homotopy of maps $u,v:P\to Q$ is a map $P\times\Delta^1\to Q$ with restrictions $u,v$ at the endpoints.

For vertices $x,y,z$ of $V_0$, let $M(x,y,z)$ be the strict fiber of $V_2\to V_0^3$ at $(x,y,z)$. The map $\theta=(d_2,d_0):M(x,y,z)\to M(x,y)\times M(y,z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration and admits a simplicial section $s$. Put $c_{x,y,z}=d_1s$. Its simplicial homotopy class is independent of $s$. These classes are associative and unital: the two composites on $M(x,y)\times M(y,z)\times M(z,w)$ are simplicially homotopic, and the maps $g\mapsto c_{x,x,y}(s_0x,g)$ and $f\mapsto c_{x,y,y}(f,s_0y)$ on $M(x,y)$ are each simplicially homotopic to its identity. On components $c$ induces composition in $hV$. For every section $s$, one has $d_1\simeq c_{x,y,z}\theta$ on $M(x,y,z)$.

If $f\in M(x,y)_0$ represents an isomorphism in $hV$, then the maps
$$f^*:M(y,z)\longrightarrow M(x,z),\quad g\longmapsto c_{x,y,z}(f,g),\qquad f_*:M(w,x)\longrightarrow M(w,y),\quad h\longmapsto c_{w,x,y}(h,f)$$
are weak homotopy equivalences for every $z,w$. Their maps on components are respectively precomposition and postcomposition by $[f]$, so both preserve and reflect invertible components.

mathlib_searches.query: Precomposition by an invertible arrow in a Segal space induces a weak equivalence of mapping spaces
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: the Segal hits concern a single strict Segal simplicial set with a bijective spine map, not a Reedy fibrant simplicial space with weakly equivalent spine mapping spaces. Read Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/StrictSegal.lean:42-57,275-325 and Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/Quasicategory/StrictSegal.lean:34-35. Ordinary category equivalences and structured-arrow precomposition do not give weak equivalences of these Kan mapping complexes.
